name: chimera-octavian-knowledge-db
notes: Curated retrieval corpus for the embedded AI module. Appending a validated entry is the learning step; no model weights are stored.

entries.summary: 64-bit ARM: 31 GPRs plus SP, EL0-EL3 exception levels, TTBR0/TTBR1 translation regimes, 4/16/64 KiB granule support.
Little-endian POWER8+: 64-bit GPRs, segment tables plus hash/page-table MMU, OPAL firmware interface for runtime services.
64-bit RISC ISA with 32 GPRs, 3 privilege levels, page-walk through CRMD/DMW registers, LoongArch Linux ABI.
Load/store RISC with delay slots, KSEG0/KSEG1 mapped segments, CP0 coprocessor for exceptions and TLB.
Open ISA: RV64I base plus M/A/F/D/C extensions; M/S/U privilege modes, satp-based Sv39/Sv48 paging, CLINT/PLIC interrupt controllers.
Supervisor Binary Interface (SBI) is the firmware/kernel contract: console putchar, IPI send, timer set, hart start, system reset.
Stack machine with a linear memory; not a boot target for Koronos, but the desktop tooling emits wasm for in-browser demos.

aarch64: assembler GNU as or LLVM MC; GCC triplet aarch64-linux-gnu; syscall entry `svc #0`; paging 4/16/64 KiB granules, TTBR0/TTBR1; boot UEFI stub + device tree, arm64 Image; ABI X0-X5 args, X8 number, SVC immediate 0.
aarch64 crosses to CPL0 with `svc #0` and keeps a per-process address space; the ABI is X0-X5 args, X8 number, SVC immediate 0.
armv7: assembler GNU as; GCC triplet arm-linux-gnueabihf; syscall entry `svc #0` (ARM and Thumb); paging 4 KiB, short-descriptor tables; boot U-Boot, device tree, zImage; ABI R0-R6 args, R7 number.
armv7 crosses to CPL0 with `svc #0` (ARM and Thumb) and keeps a per-process address space; the ABI is R0-R6 args, R7 number.

i386: assembler GNU as or NASM; GCC triplet i386-linux-gnu; syscall entry `int 0x80` / `sysenter`; paging 4 KiB pages, PAE optional; boot Multiboot 1/2, bzImage; ABI EAX number, EBX/ECX/EDX/ESI/EDI/EBP args.
i386 crosses to CPL0 with `int 0x80` / `sysenter` and keeps a per-process address space; the ABI is EAX number, EBX/ECX/EDX/ESI/EDI/EBP args.
loongarch64: assembler GNU as; GCC triplet loongarch64-linux-gnu; syscall entry `syscall 0`; paging 16 KiB pages typical; boot UEFI + device tree; ABI A0-A7 args, A7 number.
loongarch64 crosses to CPL0 with `syscall 0` and keeps a per-process address space; the ABI is A0-A7 args, A7 number.
mips64le: assembler GNU as; GCC triplet mips64el-linux-gnuabi64; syscall entry `syscall`; paging 4/16/64 KiB, TLB-based; boot U-Boot ELF, device tree; ABI A0-A3 args, V0 number.
mips64le crosses to CPL0 with `syscall` and keeps a per-process address space; the ABI is A0-A3 args, V0 number.

ppc64le: assembler GNU as; GCC triplet powerpc64le-linux-gnu; syscall entry `sc` (system call); paging Hash MMU or radix tree, 64 KiB pages typical; boot OPAL/skiboot, PPC64 ELF v2; ABI R3-R10 args, R0 number.
ppc64le crosses to CPL0 with `sc` (system call) and keeps a per-process address space; the ABI is R3-R10 args, R0 number.
riscv32: assembler GNU as; GCC triplet riscv32-linux-gnu; syscall entry `ecall`; paging Sv32 two-level paging; boot U-Boot/OpenSBI; ABI A0-A5 args, A7 number.
riscv32 crosses to CPL0 with `ecall` and keeps a per-process address space; the ABI is A0-A5 args, A7 number.

riscv64: assembler GNU as or LLVM MC; GCC triplet riscv64-linux-gnu; syscall entry `ecall` (SBI or S-mode); paging Sv39/Sv48/Sv57, 4 KiB base; boot OpenSBI + device tree, Image; ABI A0-A5 args, A7 number.
riscv64 crosses to CPL0 with `ecall` (SBI or S-mode) and keeps a per-process address space; the ABI is A0-A5 args, A7 number.
IBM Z 64-bit: 16 GPRs, dynamic address translation, channel I/O (subchannels/CCW) instead of MMIO, LPAR/z/VM virtualization.

s390x: assembler GNU as (HLASM-compatible mnemonics); GCC triplet s390x-linux-gnu; syscall entry `svc 0`; paging DAT (dynamic address translation), 4 KiB; boot zipl + LPAR/z/VM; ABI R2-R7 args, R1 number.
s390x crosses to CPL0 with `svc 0` and keeps a per-process address space; the ABI is R2-R7 args, R1 number.
sparc64: assembler GNU as; GCC triplet sparc64-linux-gnu; syscall entry `ta 0x6d` (trap always); paging 8 KiB pages, sun4v/sun4u MMU; boot OpenBoot/GRUB IEEE1275; ABI O0-O5 args, G1 number.
sparc64 crosses to CPL0 with `ta 0x6d` (trap always) and keeps a per-process address space; the ABI is O0-O5 args, G1 number.

wasm32: assembler WAT or LLVM MC; GCC triplet wasm32-unknown-unknown; syscall entry host sandbox call (no rings); paging linear memory, 64 KiB pages; boot browser/WASI host; ABI no register ABI; values on the operand stack.
wasm32 crosses to CPL0 with host sandbox call (no rings) and keeps a per-process address space; the ABI is no register ABI; values on the operand stack.
32-bit protected mode introduces segmentation, paging and the GDT/IDT; long mode requires PAE-like paging structures and EFER.LME.
64-bit extension of x86: long mode, 16 general registers, 4-level (optionally 5-level) paging, CPL0-3 privilege rings, IST stacks in the TSS.

x86_64: assembler GNU as (AT&T) or NASM (Intel); GCC triplet x86_64-linux-gnu; syscall entry `syscall` (MSR_LSTAR) / legacy `int 0x80`; paging 4 KiB pages, 4- or 5-level paging; boot GRUB Multiboot2, UEFI PE/COFF, bzImage; ABI RDX/RSI/RDI/R10/R8/R9 then stack; RCX and R11 clobbered by syscall.
x86_64 crosses to CPL0 with `syscall` (MSR_LSTAR) / legacy `int 0x80` and keeps a per-process address space; the ABI is RDX/RSI/RDI/R10/R8/R9 then stack; RCX and R11 clobbered by syscall.
ISO 9660 boot record that points the BIOS at a boot image; xorriso's -report_el_torito shows the catalog entries used for verification.
Koronos links at 0xFFFF800000000000+ and keeps user images below 0x0000800000000000 so a single PML4 split separates user and kernel space.
Transition from 32-bit protected mode to long mode: build PML4/PDPT/PD, set EFER.LME, enable CR0.PG then far-jump into a 64-bit code segment.
GRUB's Multiboot2 protocol: 32-bit entry with a magic value, information request tags, memory map, framebuffer and module tags; modules are named blobs the kernel classifies.
UEFI firmware loads PE/COFF images from the ESP; GRUB's efi.img provides the chain into Multiboot2 so one ISO boots BIOS and UEFI.
A gzip-compressed newc cpio archive the kernel unpacks into a ramfs and executes /init from; Koronos currently stages it as payload data.
Multi-profile HTML/JS desktop (Jasper/Windows-like, Gates/macOS-like, Aurora/Linux-like, Marine) rendered by WebKit in the Linux live session.
Compositor-owned input and buffers; clients speak xdg-shell. Aurora's Wayland profile is a visual skin, not a native compositor.
GTK3 window + WebKit2 WebView, undecorated fullscreen, hardware acceleration disabled for software rendering on VMs.
startx from tty1 autologin, openbox as WM, feh for wallpapers; Ctrl+Alt+F2 reaches a text console, Ctrl+Q quits the kiosk.
FADT supplies the PM1a/PM1b control values that power the machine off.
RSDP -> RSDT/XSDT -> MADT (interrupt controllers), FADT (power), DSDT (device tree); required for APIC and power management.
Per-port command list, FIS-based DMA, hot-plug via port interrupt status.
Host controller with per-port command lists and FIS packets; identify-device returns the model string used in storage inventories.
Multiboot2 framebuffer tag gives address, pitch, width/height and bpp; a linear framebuffer blitter plus an 8x16 font draws the console.
High Precision Event Timer, MMIO comparators; alternative to the PIT for calibration.
Routes PCI/legacy interrupts to LAPIC vectors; programmed through the MADT.
DMA remapping tables let the kernel confine device access to owned frames.
Message-signalled interrupts written to the LAPIC; MSI-X adds per-vector table entries.
Queue-pair based block protocol over PCIe: admin and I/O submission/completion queues, PRP/SGL data pointers, doorbell registers.
Identify Controller/Namespace, then create I/O queue pairs.
Walk bus/device/function, read vendor/device/class from config space, size BARs, assign memory windows, then bind a driver by class/vendor id.
MMCONFIG window maps 4 KiB per function; replaces legacy 0xCF8/0xCFC.
i8042 controller, scan code set 1/2, IRQ1; the classic fallback input path.
MC146818 registers 0x00-0x0D hold time and date; update-in-progress flag guards reads.
DMI tables describe the board, BIOS and memory modules.
APs start in real mode at a SIPI vector; a 16-bit trampoline switches them to long mode.
Port-mapped UART: divisor latch sets baud, line status bit 5 means transmit-hold-empty; COM1 is 0x3F8 and is the usual debug console.
CRB/TIS interface, PCR extend and seal/unseal for measured boot.
Graphics Output Protocol gives a linear framebuffer before ExitBootServices.
BOT/SCSI over xHCI bulk endpoints.
QEMU default VGA; the Multiboot2 framebuffer tag supersedes programming it directly.
Intel 8254x PCI NIC; descriptor rings, EEPROM MAC, MMIO registers.
QEMU's port 0xE9 debug console: one `outb` per character, captured with -debugcon file:...; the acceptance traces use it.
Realtek 8139 PCI NIC; simple RX/TX buffer model, common in emulators.
Paravirtual device family (net, blk, console, gpu) with split virtqueues, descriptor rings and a status handshake; the transport is PCI or MMIO.
Virtqueue-backed block device; sector reads via descriptor chains, used by QEMU images.
Virtqueue RX/TX pairs with a MAC from the device config space.
Extensible host controller: device slots, transfer rings, endpoint contexts; keyboards and mass storage are the usual first targets.
simple BPB-described filesystem used on EFI system partitions.
optical layout used by the release images; El Torito adds the boot record.
archive format of initramfs images (gzip-compressed).
journaled Linux filesystem; extent trees, 4 KiB blocks, journal replay.
read-only compressed filesystem used by the Linux live image (xz + BCJ).
source snapshot archive stored on the ISO for provenance.

PML4 -> PDPT -> PD -> PT, 9 bits per level, 4 KiB pages, NX and U/S bits per entry; CR3 holds the physical address of the active PML4.
The 8254 PIT provides a calibration heartbeat; the local APIC timer drives per-CPU preemption. Koronos uses a PIT deadline to abort runaway ring-3 processes.
Validate e_ident/e_machine/e_type, iterate PT_LOAD, honour p_vaddr/p_filesz/p_memsz, zero BSS, honour PF_W/PF_X for W^X, reject overlap and overflow.
Ring-3 code/data descriptors (DPL=3) are required before iretq can return to user mode; Koronos uses 0x1B data and 0x23 code selectors.
A DPL3 interrupt gate that saves CS, letting the kernel verify CS.RPL==3 as proof the call originated in user mode; Koronos uses it as the audit gate.
256 gates; each entry carries handler offset, segment selector, IST index and DPL. Koronos keeps ring-3 gates closed until TSS/stack/address space are ready.
Linux-style build: per-directory Kbuild fragments (obj-y/obj-m), Kconfig symbols, savedefconfig, modules_install and DESTDIR install targets.
Bitmap/buddy allocator over the Multiboot2 memory map; Koronos rejects RAM above the 4 GiB bootstrap ceiling and reserves the framebuffer range.
MSR_STAR/LSTAR/SFMASK configure the fast system-call path; SYSCALL clobbers RCX (return RIP) and R11 (RFLAGS), so user stubs must preserve them.
Priority-ordered run queues with per-CPU snapshots; `make`-time config selects round-robin vs priority mode. Linux 7.x uses EEVDF, Koronos keeps a simpler deterministic policy.
A 64-bit TSS descriptor supplies RSP0, the kernel stack used when an interrupt or syscall enters from CPL3; LTR loads the selector.
Koronos prefixes console lines ([KRN ], [RUN ], [SCH ], [MM  ], [AI  ]) so boot traces can be asserted mechanically, like dmesg tags on Linux.
ARM assembly (GAS): AArch64 entry and vector tables. Typical build: aarch64-linux-gnu-as.
Ada/SPARK ( Ravenscar profile): formal-verification friendly embedded work. Typical build: gnatmake.
No hosted libc: provide memset/memcpy/memmove, avoid TLS and constructors, and never assume a stack protector or red zone.
C (C11/C17 freestanding): kernel and userspace payloads in this tree. Typical build: gcc -ffreestanding.
-fno-exceptions -fno-rtti -fno-threadsafe-statics; avoid new/delete or provide a pool; virtual dispatch is fine but adds vtables to .rodata.
Fortran (scientific): userspace numerics, not kernel. Typical build: gfortran.
Go (runtime-based): not suitable for ring-0 without a custom runtime; userspace tooling only. Typical build: go build.
Java (JVM): CPU4096 simulator and hosted tools. Typical build: javac.
JavaScript/TypeScript (WebKit/Node): Aurora desktop shell. Typical build: node / WebKit2.
Python (CPython 3): image build, verification and knowledge tooling. Typical build: python3.
Build/verify scripts use stdlib only so CI images stay small; type hints + dataclasses keep schemas honest without dependencies.
no_std + core, panic handler, custom allocator; Linux 7.x supports Rust in drivers and core subsystems.
Rust (no_std): Linux 7.x drivers and core subsystems; not used by Koronos yet. Typical build: rustc --target <triple> -C panic=abort.
Zig (freestanding): can target bare metal via build.zig, no runtime. Typical build: zig build-obj -target x86_64-freestanding.
x86 assembly (NASM/GAS): entry stubs, GDT/TSS setup, ring-3 trampoline. Typical build: nasm -f elf64.
Linux 7.3 released 18 October 2026 (7.3.1 stable 30 October 2026); 7.2 is in stable maintenance, 6.18 and 6.12 are LTS lines.
make defconfig/menuconfig, O= out-of-tree builds, per-directory Kbuild with obj-y/obj-m, and modules_install under /lib/modules/<release>.
super_block/dentry/inode/file abstractions with per-filesystem operations vectors; page cache and writeback sit below them.
The x86 boot protocol hands the kernel a boot_params structure with memory map, initrd address and command line; bzImage is self-decompressing.
bus/driver/device matching via IDs, probe()/remove(), devres-managed resources, and module_init/module_exit registration macros.
start_kernel() sets up traps, memory, scheduler, IRQs, then rest_init() spawns PID 1 which execs /sbin/init or /init from initramfs.
Earliest Eligible Virtual Deadline First replaced CFS in 6.6+: per-task lag/virtual deadline, per-CPU runqueues, load balancing via sched domains.
Use a triplet (aarch64-linux-gnu-, riscv64-linux-gnu-, powerpc64le-linux-gnu-) with --sysroot; Debian packages gcc-<triplet>.
Flags that matter: -ffreestanding -fno-builtin -fno-stack-protector -fno-pic -fno-pie -mno-red-zone -mno-sse -mcmodel=kernel|large; link with -nostdlib.
GAS uses AT&T syntax by default (.intel_syntax available); NASM uses Intel syntax with `bits 64`, `global`, `section .text`. Koronos assembles with NASM.
Clang can build Linux and freestanding kernels; lld links faster than GNU ld, and -fuse-ld=lld is the usual switch. Cross targets use --target=<triple>.
SECTIONS, ENTRY, PHDRS and OUTPUT_FORMAT control segment layout; a kernel script pins the load address and drops .eh_frame/.comment.
objcopy converts ELF<->binary and sets arch flags; readelf -lW proves PT_LOAD flags; nm checks exported symbols in the acceptance gates.
One userspace init per boot, selected by the bootloader, running at CPL3 with its own CR3; it must emit its own readiness marker.
Koronos exposes EXIT=1, GETPID=2, YIELD=3, TIME_TICKS=4, WRITE=9 (fd 1). Linux numbers differ deliberately: no ABI compatibility is claimed.
